Sports.title: 'I would've taken a bullet for Man Utd but I'm not upset that I left - it wasn't the same'
Sports.content:
'I would've taken a bullet for Man Utd but I'm not upset that I left - it wasn't the same'

One Manchester United hero admitted the reasons why he wasn't upset by his Old Trafford departure

View 3 Images Javier Hernandez won two Premier League titles with Manchester United (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Javier Hernandez revealed his lack of sadness at leaving Manchester United was due to the significant change he witnessed at the club. The 38-year-old was largely an unknown commodity when signing for United in 2010 from boyhood club Guadalajara.

‌



However, the Mexican striker soon endeared himself to the fans by scoring 20 goals in 45 games in his first season as United captured the Premier League title. His potency in front of goal, never-say-die attitude and remarkable aerial ability despite his diminutive figure clinched his cult hero status at Old Trafford before his exit in 2015.

‌



His lack of playing time under David Moyes spelled the beginning of the end for Hernandez, who joined Real Madrid on loan in 2014. He was then made surplus to requirements by Louis van Gaal a year later and clinched a £7m move to Bayer Leverkusen.

‌



It's been over a decade since he left Manchester and Hernandez has now opened up about his departure during his appearance on Rio Ferdinand Presents. Speaking to his former United team-mate, the Atletico Dallas striker said: "It was very hard.

"Because if you gave me the chance to stay at United for most of my career, I would have taken it. The team that I played the most games for, even more than my hometown team in Mexico, is United.

Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future READ MORE :

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I am not that upset that I left. I would have taken a bullet for that team. It’s my team, Manchester United. But things weren’t the same. It’s not that I left the club that I was with; I left a different environment.

"It wasn’t the same club. With the departure, obviously, of Sir Alex Ferguson, but also David Gill and all that family structure. When I say family, it doesn’t mean that it was all nice, but there were values."

This introductory offer saves £384 compared to the standard price, with every package also providing 100 regular channels alongside free Netflix and discovery+ subscriptions.

‌



View 3 Images Javier Hernandez admitted why he wasn't upset when he left Man Utd (Image: Rio Ferdinand Presents/YouTube)

Hernandez cited his loan spell at Madrid that helped him come to terms with his later exit from United, but insisted he would have retired in Manchester if circumstances were different. He explained: "Something that helped me a little bit was [that] before I left United, I went to play for Real Madrid.

"So that gave me something like, if they don't value me in United, let me find a club. Bayer Leverkusen happened and I scored 40 goals in two seasons, playing in the Bundesliga was amazing, it was bittersweet.

Article continues below

View 3 Images The Mexican icon became a cult hero at Old Trafford (Image: Jan Kruger, Getty Images)

"But yes, realistically, I was very sad. Don’t get me wrong. I would have retired at United and I would take a bullet for that team. But it wasn’t the same team as the team that embraced me and gave me my first opportunity." Hernandez ended his United tenure with 59 goals in 157 games across all competitions.

Sports.title: Shakhtar Donetsk eye 2,000 mile trip for Champions League home games with Chelsea request
Sports.content:
Shakhtar Donetsk eye 2,000 mile trip for Champions League home games with Chelsea request

Shakhtar Donetsk have qualified for the Champions League this season and are hoping to use Chelsea's Stamford Bridge for their home matches in the competition

View 2 Images The logo of the UEFA Champions League is seen on a match ball (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Shakhtar Donetsk are believed to be looking at using Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea, for their home fixtures in the Champions League this season. The Ukrainian club have qualified for the competition, while the Londoners will have no European football on offer this term.

‌



The Donbass Arena, the home stadium for Shakhtar, has not been used for the club’s home matches since Russia annexed the Ukrainian city back in 2014. The 52,000-seater stadium, which is approximately 2,000 miles away from London, hosted several matches at Euro 2012 two years earlier.

‌



As a result, Shakhtar have been forced to play their home matches at Kyiv and Lviv in Ukraine instead, while Germany, Slovenia and Poland have hosted matches in European competitions.

‌

As reported by football.london, Shakhtar would not comment on the reports, stating that an official announcement would be made next week.

‌



According to the BBC, Chelsea have made it clear this move has nothing to do with commercial motives for the club. It is also understood that Brentford's G-Tech Community Stadium and Fulham's Craven Cottage were considered as potential alternative venues.

Nevertheless, Stamford Bridge is believed to be the front-runner owing to its greater capacity. Furthermore, Chelsea share a warm relationship with Shakhtar, which dates back to the transfer of Mykhailo Mudryk.

Additionally, approximately 32,000 Ukraine-born residents are thought to live in London, making Stamford Bridge an ideal venue to draw those supporters to matches - a further 100,000 people of Ukrainian descent are also believed to reside in the capital.

‌

In 2023, Stamford Bridge hosted the Game4Ukraine charity fixture, which raised funds for rebuilding the Mykhailo-Kotsiubynsky School in Chernihiv Oblast, which had been hit by Russian missiles.

‌



Last season, Shakhtar progressed to the semi-final of the Europa League, where they were eliminated by Crystal Palace. Despite the setback, it represented a remarkable accomplishment given they had no permanent home venue.

They clinched an automatic berth in next season's Champions League after Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal both qualified through their domestic league positions. This opened up a route for Ukraine to enter the league phase after they led the UEFA coefficient rankings, finishing 9.75 points clear of second-placed Crvena Zvezda.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are absent from European competition this season following last term's 10th-place finish in the Premier League. This makes the possibility of Shakhtar using Stamford Bridge more straightforward, as there should be fewer scheduling issues.

Sports.title: Man City title winner backs Arsenal to become champions again in telling admission
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City and England star Joleon Lescott doesn't expect his former club to reel in Arsenal in this season's title race. The Gunners were run close by City last season but ended the campaign seven points clear after their rivals fell away in May.

An injury to William Saliba has brought questions about the holders' hopes of retaining their title, while Elliot Anderson's move to the Etihad Stadium ought to strengthen the chasers. The departure of legendary manager Pep Guardiola also brings uncertainty in the blue half of Manchester, though, prompting Lescott to tip Arsenal to go back-to-back.

"It is very early [to make predictions], but you would say Arsenal," Lescott exclusively told Mirror Football a t TNT Sports' 'Levels' Trophy Cabinet pop-up in London. "Considering the key factors, they probably have fewer obstacles ahead of them.

"[Mikel] Arteta has continuity with the players and the squad now has genuine belief, so I would say Arsenal. I know how difficult it is to win back-to-back titles, so that is my overriding opinion."

‌

Guardiola spent a decade in Manchester, so he will naturally have big shoes to fill. Enzo Maresca can at least point to his knowledge of the City Football Group set-up, having previously led an Under-21 squad including Cole Palmer and James Trafford to Premier League 2 glory.

Maresca will show what he can do in this weekend's Community Shield and Lescott believes the appointment makes a lot of sense. "There were obviously names being speculated about but in terms of the fit, he knows the club, he knows a lot of the players," he said.

"There was always going to be some form of transition when Pep left but there are probably less factors to go wrong with Enzo, so it made sense to me. Having relationships with the club, understanding how they work, and having a connection with the players, which is very important nowadays, so it was the right appointment."

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel still has three Man Utd rules to follow despite Premier League ban being lifted
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel still has three Man Utd rules to follow despite Premier League ban being lifted

JJ Gabriel is officially eligible to play in the Premier League this season, but several rules remain in place for the Manchester United youngster

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is able to play in the Premier League this season (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel is no longer bound by his Premier League ban but still must abide by three Manchester United rules. The 15-year-old starlet made his unofficial club debut in United's pre-season friendly victory against Atletico Madrid earlier this month.

‌



He became the youngest-ever player to feature in the first team after coming on for Bryan Mbeumo in the 82nd minute. More senior appearances for the club could be on the cards for the attacker this season.

‌



Gabriel turns 16 in October, which means he'll be eligible to make his top-flight debut in the upcoming campaign. However, he'll still need to follow three United rules because of his age.

‌



One of those strict rules leaves the teenager unable to wear the club's new training kit sponsor because of gambling regulations. The Red Devils recently inked a £20million per year deal with Betway, as the gambling company now sponsors United's training wear.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gabriel, alongside every other under-18 player in the Premier League, is not allowed to wear club gear that promotes gambling companies. United's multi-million-pound deal came in spite of the top-flight's impending rule in the 2026/27 season that bans betting firms from being the front-of-shirt sponsors for clubs.

‌



The rule was first agreed in April 2023, but the ban doesn't stop betting companies from being featured on shirt sleeves and training kits, as well as appearing in stadiums.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel made his unofficial Manchester United debut earlier this month (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Gabriel also remains banned from getting dressed in United's first-team changing rooms. The youngster is separated from his team-mates before and after a game as Premier League regulations state that any player under 18 years old must change in a separate area from the senior squad, for both training sessions and matches.

Gabriel will be able to enter the changing room after his team-mates are dressed in order to United boss Michael Carrick give his team talks. And the youngster is also blocked from signing a professional deal.

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer news: Bradley Barcola boost as club agree to lower asking price
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer news: Bradley Barcola boost as club agree to lower asking price

Liverpool's Premier League opener against Newcastle United is one week away but the club still have plenty to do in the transfer market

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola's first Premier League match as Liverpool boss is a week away (Image: Getty)

Andoni Iraola's first Premier League season as Liverpool boss is just around the corner and he has welcomed three senior summer signings so far. However, there could still be more to come.

‌



Having supplanted Arne Slot, Iraola's debut pre-season has not entirely gone according to plan on the pitch, with two wins against Sunderland and Wrexham and two losses against Leeds and Monaco. But off the field, their transfer business has been shrewd.

‌



Victor Munoz's Osasuna release clause was activated and he joined for £34.6million. Soon after, Jeremy Jacquet's £60m transfer was completed following negotiations in January. Ronald Araujo is the latest arrival from Barcelona after a loan deal with an option to buy for £47.1m was completed.

‌



However, a winger is still the Reds' priority and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola tops that list. The deal continues to be complicated, but Liverpool have received a telling double boost. Mirror Football brings you the latest transfer updates from Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool finally change transfer stance after breakthrough in negotiations READ MORE :

Bradley Barcola boost

It is understood that Liverpool's pursuit of Barcola has been a cagey one to date. Preliminary talks have been completed with the player's team and various reports suggest a bid is imminent.

‌



View 3 Images Barcola has some new team-mates (Image: Getty)

However, PSG's asking price, thought to be £130m, has been deemed too high. Nevertheless, the Parisian side have announced the arrival of a new winger and are all set to confirm the signing of another.

World Cup winner Ferran Torres has joined PSG from Barcelona for £42m and young Mika Godts will soon be signed from Ajax for £48m. The pair will join Maghnes Akliouche as attacking summer arrivals.

‌



This double deal surely indicates that Barcola will soon find himself surplus to requirements and essentially confirms that PSG intend to sell him this summer. Whether their asking price is lowered, though, is another matter.

Godts and Torres being snapped up could also provide the Reds with a boost regarding Ibrahim Mbaye. Reports in France suggest a deal for the 18-year-old Senegal international is still on and Liverpool may also make a move for him.

Sports.title: Precise faces More Thunder in Prix Jacques le Marois
Sports.content:
Precise, More Thunder and Zeus Olympios line up for the 2026 Prix Jacques Le Marois, live on Sky Sports Racing.

2.50 Deauville - Precise takes on More Thunder and Zeus Olympios in Prix Jacques le Marois

Star filly Precise takes on More Thunder and Zeus Olympios in a very competitive renewal of the The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois.

Four-time Group 1 winner Precise has built herself a very nice profile, having backed up a pair of Group 1 wins at two with victories in the Irish 1000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes. She has since been beaten twice since stepping into open company, being downed by the Juddmonte-owned Blue Bolt on both occasions. The fillies' allowance could prove crucial here and with Ryan Moore on board, she is in the right hands.

More Thunder will look to reverse the form with Zeus Olympios, with the latter much the best when last seen in Ascot's Summer Mile. Karl Burke's charge got the run of the race that day, scooting clean under Sam James. William Haggas' representative was second in Group 1 company twice prior and, like Zeus Olympios, will look to take top honours for the first time today.

Thesecretadversary is a recent Group 1 scorer in the Prix Jean Prat, which followed a win at the Royal meeting in the Jersey Stakes. He was originally targeted towards the City Of York Stakes but has since been rerouted after Bow Echo and Gstaad were retired and ruled out respectively.

Rayif looks the best of the French contenders but will have to bounce back after disappointing when sent off a 6/4 favourite in the Prix Jean Prat. The step back up to a mile could prove crucial for Mickael Barzalona's mount, who tasted success over the mile in the French 2000 Guineas earlier this season.

1.33 Deauville - Exciting Avec Toi faces Silver Dominion in Group 3 company

The much talked about Avec Toi faces just four runners in this Group 3 The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin.

Christopher Head has said the target this season for this son of No Nay Never is the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere on Arc weekend and he looks to be a special talent from his outings thus far. He arrives here with two wins from as many starts, with a debut win at Saint-Cloud followed up by a sparkling showing over this course and distance the last day.

In opposition, Silver Dominion brings stakes form to the table. Oliver Cole's runner finished second in the Pat Eddery Stakes last time after a fourth-place finish in the Superlative Stakes on July Cup day and could give the favourite a real run for his money.

Godolphin's Jassas looked promising when winning on debut at Doncaster - a result which has seen the form boosted this week with runner-up Narrjoo winning at Ffos Las on Wednesday. Zakkan cannot be discounted for the formidable Graffard and Barzalona combination despite being winless in three, whilst Cut A Dash completes the quintet and looks to have plenty to find on the rest of the field.

2.35 Southwell - 750,000gns Godolphin yearling Palladas returns

Expensive yearling Palladas returns to the track for the LNAA Critical Care Novice Stakes after being absent since beating Al Azd at Kempton in January.

The form from this maiden victory has produced seven individual winners - most notably Al Azd, who is now rated 109. Roger Varian's Shadwell gelding was sixth in the London Gold Cup and second in the King George V Stakes before hosing up at Ascot in a class 2 handicap. That form line would suggest a lofty ceiling for Charlie Appleby's runner today, who will be partnered by the title-chasing Billy Loughnane.

Theory Of Tides' half-brother Mercantile debuts for Daniel and Clare Kubler and is of interest first time out, but this should really be a one-horse race.

Best of the rest

Back at Deauville, Listed winner Romantic Symphony goes in search of Group 3 honours in the The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly. She will be rivalled by Calandagan's half-sister Calasita, who holds an entry in the Champions Fillies And Mares Stakes and was only half a length behind Romantic Symphony last time. Dispatches drops down into Group 3 company under Colin Keane, whilst Hatanka Fal has been there or thereabouts at Listed level but must improve to go close today.

At Southwell, Astrological looks to carry a 6lb penalty to success in the Newark Advertiser Handicap (1.30pm) before Valvano and Legal Reform clash in the Coopers Marquees Handicap at 3.40pm.

Sports.title: Scheffler retains lead in Memphis as Burns stars and McIlroy toils again
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler will take a two-shot lead into the final round of the FedEx St Jude Championship in Memphis as he looks to complete his first win since January.

The three-stroke advantage the world No 1 had carved out at halfway after a second-round, course-record 61 was trimmed by one as he bogeyed his penultimate hole at TPC Southwind on Saturday before signing for a two-under 68 and closing on 13 under.

Sam Burns carded a sizzling, bogey-free eight-under 62 while Sungjae Im shot a three-under 67 with those players the leader's closest challengers on 11 under.

But Scheffler is now just one good day away from his maiden trophy since The American Express in California at the start of the year, not that he hasn't threatened in that time.

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work? Only the top 70 in the season-long FedExCup standings have reached the FedEx St. Jude Championship. The top 50 then progress to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 make it to the Tour Championship (August 27-30). Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship. In the closing event, all players begin at even par, with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025. The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

The 30-year-old has recorded five runners-up finishes, including at the 3M Open in his previous event, and nine top-fives in total in the intervening months.

In his third round in Tennessee, Scheffler bogeyed his fourth hole before birdies at two, 11, 12 and 16 preceded that dropped shot at 17, which came after he picked out a left-hand bunker with his second shot at the par four.

Defending FedExCup Playoffs champion Tommy Fleetwood remains in the hunt after a two-under Saturday - the highlight of which was a monster birdie putt at 13 - leaving him five strokes adrift of Scheffler on eight under and in a share of fourth with Jake Knapp.

Image: Rory McIlroy has not shot a round under par at TPC Southwind this week

Rory McIlroy, though, is languishing in tied-67th place on six over - 19 shots off Scheffler - after shooting a two-over 72 on Saturday, with the world No 2 yet to post an under-par round this week.

McIlroy, a three-time FedExCup Playoffs champion, was even par on the day heading to the 18th in his third round, only to then finish with a double bogey after finding the water off the tee.

The 37-year-old picked up back-to-back birdies at nine and 10, while his bogeys came at two and 13 before his gory final hole.

Sports.title: Djokovic knocked out early in Cincinnati after struggling in sapping heat
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic suffered defeat and struggled physically in his first match since Wimbledon as he was upset by Thiago Agustin Tirante in a sapping three-set contest at the Cincinnati Open.

Djokovic, inactive on the ATP Tour since losing to Jannik Sinner at the grass-court Grand Slam on July 10, won the first set 6-2 but then lost the next two 6-4 as he battled the heat and humidity in Ohio, even appearing to vomit at one stage.

The 24-time major champion won an 18-minute third game of the second set, fending off four break points over nine deuces, before taking a medical timeout, while he dropped to his hands and knees at certain points in a match that lasted two hours and 45 minutes.

Tirante revels in 'best win of career'

Tirante, who can look forward to a third-round meeting with Spain's Martin Landaluce, made the decisive break at 4-4 in the decider after converting his fourth break point of the game and then closed out the win on serve.

Image: Tirante says his win over Djokovic was the best of his career

He said afterwards: "This is the best win of my career. I really did a good job inside the court. I managed very well the nerves of playing against a legend like Novak. Now I feel relieved.

"It is all so much pressure when you cannot break [serve]. I had so many points to break and I couldn't, so that was the key. Keep believing in myself with my team and think about it after the match."

Djokovic was the third seed in Cincinnati despite sitting fifth in the world rankings, with world No 1 Sinner withdrawing due to a knee injury and world No 3 Carlos Alcaraz also absent as he continues to deal with a lingering wrist issue.

Top seed Alexander Zverev plays Britain's Cameron Norrie in the second round overnight.

Sports.title: St Helens keep slim play-off hopes alive by stunning Wakefield
Sports.content:
St Helens produced a blistering second-half performance to stun Wakefield Trinity with a 46-16 victory and keep their slim Super League play-off hopes alive.

Saints, who have never failed to make the post-season, came into the match on a run of three defeats in a row and five losses in six, leaving them six points off the top six.

The visitors slipped 10-0 down to fourth-placed Wakefield and trailed 16-12 at half-time but then ran in six unanswered tries in the second period.

Wakefield falter after bright start

Wakefield, who lost Josh Rourke and try-scorer Isaiah Vagana to injuries inside the first quarter of an hour, missed the chance to move two points behind table toppers Leeds as they suffered a sixth successive defeat to Saints and slipped to back-to-back home losses after last week's narrow reverse against the Rhinos.

Tyson Smoothy's eighth-minute effort, which was converted by Jack Sinfield, and Vagana's Sinfield-aided score in the 12th put Wakefield on top.

However, Vagana was barged into as he went down and went off with a physio holding his left arm, after Rourke departed following a collision with Murphy.

Image: St Helens kept their play-off hopes alive

Sailor and Murphy dragged Saints back into the contest with tries that Jackson Hastings converted, only for Sinfield to exploit a huge gap before kicking his second conversion to leave Wakefield four points to the good at the break.

Lachlan Walmsley had two tries chalked off for Trinity after the resumption, either side of which Murphy put Saints back in front with another fine finish, diving one-handed in the corner before hobbling off with an injury to his left leg.

Once Billy Keeley latched on to a loose ball and went over after 64 minutes, Saints dominated, with Sailor's hat-trick, sealed after a lung-busting run, prompting Wakefield's fans to stream for the exits.

"It's hugely disappointing and I've said to the players 'we've got to flip this pretty quick'. We play Wigan next week and it doesn't get any harder than that."

Wigan level on points with Leeds as Bradford slip to bottom spot

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Bradford Bulls and Wigan Warriors

Wigan moved level on points with leader Leeds as they scored six tries in a 34-6 victory at lowly Bradford, who now prop up the table following resurgent Huddersfield's victory at Toulouse on Saturday evening.

The visitors crossed three times in each half with Jake Wardle, Adam Keighran and Bevan French touching down before the break.

Wardle went over again in the second period while Kian McDermott and Jake Kerr also registered tries, with the Bulls' sole effort coming from Andy Ackers.

Wigan's 18th win of the season leaves them four points clear of Warrington and Wakefield in third and fourth respectively, while Bradford have been usurped by Huddersfield on points difference after their fellow Yokshiremen's 26-10 win in France.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League game between the Toulouse Olympique and the Huddersfield Giants

The Giants have won four games in a row after just two victories across their first 19 matches, with this latest success thanks to two tries from Sam Halsall and one apiece for Joe Greenwood and Conor Wrench.

Huddersfield's revival, which has also included beating York, Hull FC and Catalans, has come at the same time Toulouse have faded, with Sylvain Houles' men on a four-match losing streak following previous disappointing results against Catalans, Leeds and Wigan.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: SunRisers, Super Giants out to deny Rockets a Hundred double
Sports.content:
There could be a Trent Rockets double and a Sam Billings four-peat at Lord's on Sunday as the 2026 edition of The Hundred draws to a close.

Rockets' men's and women's sides advanced directly to the finals after topping their respective tables during the group phase, winning 13 of their combined 16 matches.

The Midlanders already have the Hundred Helix trophy sewn up - a new prize awarded to the best-performing franchise across the men's and women's competitions.

Image: Trent Rockets won the Hundred Helix trophy with both of their teams reaching Sunday's finale at Lord's

Now, though, Rockets, want to secure individual men's and women's glory, live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Mix.

The women are up first at the Home of Cricket as they take on defending champions SunRisers Leeds from 2.15pm - SunRisers triumphed a year ago under their Northern Superchargers name - before the men play Manchester Super Giants from 6pm.

Rockets women have never won The Hundred before. In fact, this is their first final, after four group-stage exits and a defeat in the eliminator across the first five editions.

Rockets men, meanwhile, are one-time champions, prevailing in 2022 before their now-captain Billings began his love affair with this tournament and led Oval Invincibles to three successive Hundred titles, capped off with a win over Rockets in the 2025 final.

Image: Sam Billings captained Oval Invincibles to three successive Hundred titles from 2023 to 2025 and is looking to add to that run with Rockets

Billings 'very proud' of Hundred success

Invincibles let Billings go ahead of the auction as they began a new era under their MI London moniker, allowing Rockets to swoop for him. It has been an extremely shrewd acquisition, with Billings now on the brink of four in a row.

The Rockets skipper said: "It is impressive. It's something I'm very proud of and to have the opportunity to win another one, albeit with a different team, is very pleasing. You want to be in this stage of the tournament every year so it's not lost on me.

"The opportunity we have, I never take it for granted, playing here at the Home of Cricket. As a young kid growing up, you dream of occasions like this and playing at Lord's. As you get older, you start to appreciate these things a little more, I suppose.

"I think we might be one of the oldest teams in the competition. We have a lot of guys who have played in finals before, been successful in finals. We have had brilliant energy throughout this competition."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester Super Giants' Jos Buttler hit a massive six in the win over SunRisers Leeds in the eliminator before being dismissed next ball

Billings' opposite number on Sunday will be Jos Buttler, who has stepped up to captain Super Giants since South Africa's Aiden Markram exited for personal reasons.

Buttler has stepped up with the bat, too - plundering 311 runs, including four fifties, and he cracked 33 off 20 balls in the eliminator win over SunRisers on Friday night.

Billings, whose side beat Super Giants by six wickets while amid a run of six straight wins during the group stage, said of his weekend opponents: "They're a very good team.

"Jos [Buttler] is arguably the best white-ball player ever to represent England and the leading record run-scorer ever in T20 cricket. They've got a lot of variety in their side as well. But I think it's all about us, to be honest.

"We topped the group. We beat them in Manchester, which definitely gives us confidence. We will absolutely respect them. But, as a team, winning the league stage gives us a lot of confidence. We've been the best team from a record point of view."

Image: Billings (right) says it is 'preferable' to have topped the league stage so that his team got more of a rest than Super Giants before the final

Can Gibson's SunRisers deny Gardner more Lord's glory?

There will definitely be a triumphant England captain in the men's final, either Billings or Buttler, and there could also be one in the women's.

SunRisers' Dani Gibson - one of only three English skippers in the women's competition this term, alongside London Spirit's Charlie Dean and MI London's Hollie Armitage - will be hoping to get the better of Rockets' Australian leader Ash Gardner.

Gibson was in the England team beaten by an Australian outfit containing Gardner in the Women's T20 World Cup final at Lord's in July.

Gardner also has fellow 2026 World Cup winners Kim Garth and Beth Mooney with her at Rockets, although there are members of that victorious squad in the SunRisers' ranks in Phoebe Litchfield and Annabel Sutherland, the leading run-scorers in the women's Hundred this term.

The performances throughout the competition have shown that it's not the same people standing up every game. We've got a lot of experience and that really helps in a fast-paced format where you're under pressure quickly. Players have stayed composed in those moments and we've also got people willing to take the game on.

Gardner said: "There are definitely some fantastic memories here at Lord's. It's nice coming back to the same dressing room and hopefully that brings some good energy. Having a few Australians in the side helps because we know what big occasions require.

"Sunday is a new game and a different challenge but there are plenty of positive memories to draw on and confidence in the things we've done well throughout the season."

Gibson added of playing Rockets, who have England skipper Nat Sciver-Brunt in their line-up: "They've got some great names but I think every team has great names. It's just making sure that we prep well and play the conditions that we're going to get here.

"Adapt quickly, communicate well and enjoy playing."

Watch The Hundred finals, at Lord's, live from 2pm on Sunday on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Mix. The women's match between Trent Rockets and SunRisers Leeds starts at 2.15pm with the men's between Trent Rockets and Manchester Super Giants under way at 6pm. Stream cricket contract-free with NOW.

Sports.title: Community Shield offers insight into Arsenal’s desire and Maresca’s Manchester City impact | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
The doubt for anyone when a long-strived-for goal has been achieved is hunger. Arsenal waited 22 years for their 14th league title and, compounding the yearning, finished second three times in a row before finally lifting the Premier League trophy in May. The physical exertions of last season were immense – as seen by Declan Rice’s clear exhaustion and Bukayo Saka’s intermittent contributions at the World Cup, where William Saliba picked up a back injury – but so too was the emotional strain.

The first weeks of a new season after a major tournament, especially the World Cup, are often a little erratic anyway, but this feels like a particularly unpredictable start to a campaign. Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs have changed manager this summer. For the first time in 40 years, none of the five big managerial beasts of the Premier League era – Sir Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola – will be in charge of a club. There are unknowns and uncertainty everywhere, even at Arsenal. Mikel Arteta may be the longest-serving manager in the league but there are questions even there; it would be no great surprise if Arsenal were to start slowly.

Manchester City are at the other end of the scale, after two seasons that were disappointing by their extremely elevated recent standards, and with a new manager after a decade under Guardiola. Enzo Maresca may look like his predecessor and his football may look like a version of his predecessor’s – notably from that period when he was his assistant manager – but he arrives at City surrounded by questions. He led Leicester to promotion and won the Europa Conference League and Club World Cup with Chelsea, but fans of those clubs seemed unconvinced by the style of play. And while Chelsea clearly had problems with the balance of their squad, and got dramatically worse after he left, it wasn’t entirely clear he was making the best of the resources he had.

The Community Shield is a first opportunity to make some kind of assessment of whether Arsenal’s hunger is as sharp as it was last season, and of how City’s squad are adapting to their new manager. It is, though, a largely ceremonial occasion, any lessons drawn to be taken with extreme caution. Not since 2018 have the winners of the Community Shield gone on to win the Premier League; in that sense, it’s a sort of anti-bellwether. Where it can give indicators as to the season ahead tends to be less in showcasing the strengths of a potential champion than in exposing the flaws that might bring a side low.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca looks like his predecessor, and his football can resemble some of Pep Guardiola’s, but he has challenges to overcome. Photograph: Lee Jin-man/AP

This year is unlikely to bring a repeat of 1974, when the scrap between Kevin Keegan and Billy Bremner exposed both the Liverpool forward’s unease at the retirement of Bill Shankly and, more consequentially, the general loss of morale at Leeds after Brian Clough had succeeded Don Revie. Often the significance of the Community Shield is properly recognised only in retrospect. José Mourinho was clearly in a strange mood when he turned up for the 2015-16 game unshaven and in tracksuit bottoms and a baggy T-shirt before suffering his first ever defeat to Arsène Wenger. Few suspected, though, the chaos that was about to unspool at Chelsea, culminating with Mourinho’s dismissal that December.

Last season, as Crystal Palace beat Liverpool on penalties after a 2-2 draw, there were abundant indications of what was to come, especially about Arne Slot’s side. Mohamed Salah seemed disconnected from the rest of the forward line. The defence was a mess. Twice they conceded equalisers. Whether they were recognised at the time is another matter; the difficulty is separating teething problems or a team being only partway through their preparation for the new season from longer-term issues that could still be undermining a team two or three months into the season.

There are few obvious questions to which Sunday’s meeting could begin to offer answers. Bruno Guimarães came off the bench for Arsenal in Wednesday’s friendly against Como and could be involved, probably alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield. The 19-year-old has been prominent in pre-season after Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Martin Ødegaard were given extended breaks after the World Cup, but he has been linked with a move. In that context, his celebration after scoring against Como, making a heart sign with his hands and tapping the badge, felt significant.

After the sale of Leandro Trossard, the left side of Arsenal’s attack is in need of strengthening. Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea and Vinícius Júnior stayed at Real Madrid, but they did sign the 24-year-old Greece international Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. Sunday offers an opportunity to see how he fits in, and whether Arsenal still need another option on that flank.

For City, the biggest personnel issue probably surrounds the future of Rodri, whose proposed move to Barcelona is yet to materialise, which in turn leaves City hanging on a potential replacement. Enzo Fernández appears the preferred candidate but whether his comparative lack of physicality can be accommodated deep in midfield, even after the signing of the robust Elliot Anderson, remains to be seen.

View image in fullscreen Phil Foden, pictured in action against Atlético Madrid during their recent friendly, has a chance to reassert himself. Photograph: Chung Sung-Jun/Getty Images

Tijjani Reijnders started friendlies against Inter and Atlético but is on his way to Al-Qadsiah while Bernardo Silva has joined Real Madrid, meaning a significant overhaul of midfield. Whether that includes Phil Foden in the long term is unclear. Since being named player of the year in 2024, he has struggled for form, but started the Inter and Atlético games. As others recover from the World Cup, the next few weeks offer an opportunity to reassert himself.

Given he started only 11 games over the past two seasons, the departure of John Stones probably matters less from a footballing point of view than in the loss of a dressing-room leader. Without Stones and Silva – and Guardiola – the character of the squad cannot but be different.

Sunday constitutes an opportunity to see both what the new City may look like, and how Arsenal have adapted, having at last won the title. But it’s only the Community Shield; any conclusions should be treated with appropriate caution.

Sports.title: Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle looks on bright side despite lacklustre Leverkusen defeat
Sports.content:
Reasons to be fearful or cause to be cheerful? Newcastle fans among a crowd in excess of 39,000 at St James’ Park on Saturday had much to debate as they headed home from a slightly underwhelming 2-1 friendly defeat by Bayer Leverkusen.

The bad news is that a suddenly youthful team still coming to terms with life without this summer’s departed stars, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, look more than a little undercooked before Liverpool’s visit on Premier League duty next Sunday.

Late last year these teams drew a Champions League group stage game in Leverkusen but since then the Germans have reconstructed a then transitional squad and Newcastle dismantled theirs.

Eddie Howe’s sudden departure at the end of July has left Matthias Jaissle, late of Jeddah’s Al-Ahli, to pick up the managerial pieces. Despite this defeat on a day when Leverkusen looked to be playing within themselves, the 38-year-old German is already showing a few, albeit tentative, indications that he just might be able to put one of football’s most complicated jigsaws back together.

If Malick Thiaw, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa in particular appear re-energised by his coaching, Jaissle’s faith in the 17-year-old Mason Miley, the younger brother of the midfielder Lewis, was fully vindicated as the academy product shone at right-back.

“Mason’s a young lad with the attitude we need; he has the right heart and the right quality,” said Jaissle as he sipped an energy drink intended to replace the body’s lost electrolytes. If only he could find such a simple solution to filling the missing links left by Gordon, Tonali and Guimarães.

At least Dan Burn is still around and will be Newcastle’s captain, with Joelinton as his deputy. The Brazilian, though, is injured and will miss the Liverpool game, while Burn was not involved here as Jaissle split his squad in two during a weekend that features another friendly here, against Strasbourg on Sunday.

Leverkusen represented the new manager’s first match in charge at St James’ Park but it was hardly the ideal start. Inside a minute his team were behind.

When Ibrahim Maza manoeuvred the ball on to his left foot in the area, Newcastle’s new goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, was powerless to resist the resultant shot. No matter that it was only a friendly, even Howe’s normally super-confident successor looked a little crestfallen.

“It’s a big challenge,” he said. “It’s a big transition.”

Jaissle cut a restless figure as he prowled the home technical area, sometimes straying far too far outside its confines for the liking of match officials.

View image in fullscreen Yoane Wissa shoots in Newcastle’s home strip before they switched to lilac shirts, due to a colour clash, at the first hydration break. Photograph: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images

The good news for a coach who promises to prove more entertaining than his team – at least in their current incarnation – was that a reasonably strong starting XI improved incrementally during the first half and equalised shortly before half-time. Jaissle duly greeted Thiaw’s scoring header from Elanga’s corner with a prolonged bout of clapping.

By then he could also reflect favourably on a positive contribution from the Miley brothers. While Lewis looked his customarily assured self in central midfield on his first appearance since breaking a leg last spring, Mason’s efforts at right-back frequently frustrated Leverkusen’s Miguel Gutiérrez.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It seemed thoroughly fitting that the latter was showered with praise from his manager when, late in the second half, he hobbled off with cramp. With England’s Tino Livramento sidelined by calf trouble, Miley Jr is in real contention to start against Liverpool.

Yet in eight days’ time another right-back, Benfica’s Amar Dedic, could well have been added to Newcastle’s squad. The 23-year-old, who can also operate at left-back, previously played for Jaissle at RB Salzburg and, on Saturday night, appeared close to finalising a move to Tyneside.

Once that deal is done attention will doubtless turn to filling the midfield chasm left by Tonali and Guimarães. Although the 18-year-old Sean Steur – one of four players aged 20 or under signed by Newcastle since June – showed off some nice touches, the former Ajax prodigy betrayed his inexperience at times.

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is still working out how best to fit together the pieces of the Newcastle jigsaw. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Players with more mature presence are clearly required but Marseille’s Pierre-Emile Højbjerg has declined a £13m move to north-east England and João Palhinha is still to be persuaded to leave Bayern Munich to plug the leadership vacuum.

On this evidence Leverkusen’s new manager, Carles Martínez, recently imported from Toulouse, might be reluctant to do a job swap with his Newcastle counterpart. Martínez’s side improved after the second-half introduction of the dangerous forward Patrik Schick and few Newcastle fans would argue the visitors did not deserve to win courtesy of Victor Boniface’s late rolled finish, with that opening created when the Nigerian expertly turned Steur.

How Jaissle, who looks to still be fathoming out how to unlock Nick Woltemade’s real yet still latent talent, could do with similar attacking incision.

Asked if Liverpool were arriving in Toon too soon, he initially replied: “We’ll do our best,” before turning upbeat. “We’ll keep using positivity,” he said. “I like these challenges. We are not concerned. I can’t wait.”

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Middlesbrough seal comeback win; West Brom beat Norwich
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear scored a second-half double on his debut as Middlesbrough fought back to kick off their Championship campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 victory, ending promoted Lincoln’s remarkable nine-month unbeaten run.

The Imps – playing their first second-tier match in 65 years – made a strong start and opened the scoring in the 12th minute through Adam Reach. But the former Tottenham forward Lankshear marked his first league appearance since his move to the Riverside by equalising just after the hour and then stabbing in a stoppage-time winner.

It was a devastating end for Lincoln as a run of 29 games undefeated in all competitions since early December was brought to a halt in their first league match since their new joint head coach partnership of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw stepped up to take over after the departure of Michael Skubala to Bristol City in May.

Philippe Clement was left feeling extremely hard done by after watching his Norwich side lose 2-1 at home to West Brom. Clement felt his side should have won the game comfortably with the number of chances they created – and also felt Aune Heggebø’s opener, which came against the run of play, should have been ruled out for handball.

“It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,” he said. “It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted. There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn’t have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that. Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn’t happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.”

View image in fullscreen Aune Heggebø (right) appeared to score West Brom’s opener against Norwich with his arm. Photograph: Paul Chesterton/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Norwich were on the front foot for most of the game but could not find a way past a resolute defence, and were made to pay for failing to take their chances as Albion scored two late goals to make it a dream start to the new season.

The visitors went in front on 75 minutes when Callum Styles played in Jimmy-Jay Morgan, whose cross was bundled over the line by Heggebø. With three minutes remaining, Morgan made it two with his third goal since joining the Baggies in the summer, racing clear and working his way into the box before blasting the ball home. Mathias Kvistgaarden nodded home a loose ball as the game entered added time.

Ilias Chair scored twice as QPR came from behind to beat Portsmouth 3-1 and claim their first win at Fratton Park in 26 years. Pompey dominated the opening half an hour and took the lead through Terry Devlin’s long-range screamer. But Rangers scored three times in 15 minutes before half-time.

Quick Guide League One: Lowe penalty gives Wednesday winning start Show Jamal Lowe converted a second-half penalty as Sheffield Wednesday made a winning start in League One following relegation with a 2-1 victory at Leyton Orient. The Owls, under new ownership since succumbing to the earliest relegation in English Football League history in February, went ahead through Callum Slattery’s debut goal before Joseph Olowu levelled before the break. But Lowe picked himself up after being fouled in the area by James Morris to fire home from the spot in the 66th minute. Former Premier League champions Leicester were denied victory at Notts County in their first match since relegation as they were held 1-1. Conor Grant’s late strike cancelled out Jayden Joseph’s second-half opener for Leicester and salvaged a deserved point for the home side. Ciaron Brown’s stoppage-time equaliser rescued another relegated side, Oxford, earning them a 2-2 draw at newly-promoted MK Dons. Charlie Goode and Aaron Collins gave the Dons a 2-1 half-time lead after Mark Harris had fired the U’s in front before Brown turned home a cross in the fifth minute of added time. Substitute Gideon Kodua scrambled a stoppage-time winner to seal Luton a 4-3 win at Reading, for whom Jack Marriott scored a first-half hat-trick. Huddersfield’s summer signing Derensili Sanches Fernandes struck twice as they beat AFC Wimbledon 3-0 at home despite the first-half dismissal of Bali Mumba. Victor Adeboyejo fired a second-half winner as Bromley won 1-0 at Barnsley for their first-ever win in the third tier following promotion. Cambridge United held off a fightback to beat Wigan 3-2 on the U’s return to League One. Goals from Kell Watts, Louis Appere and Isaac Heath put the hosts in control but Wigan made a game of it in the last 20 minutes when Sonny Perkins and Akeel Higgins set up a nervy finish. Blackpool and Wycombe shared the points in an opening day 1-1 draw. The visitors led for long periods at Bloomfield Road, following an early opener from Fred Onyedinma. This was cancelled out by substitute Finley Munroe, who made an instant impact following his loan move from Middlesbrough last week. Bradford made a winning start with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Peterborough, who finished with 10 men after David Okagbue’s red card. Second-half goals from Macaulay Gillesphey and Nick Powell were enough for last season’s play-off semi-finalists to secure three points. Stockport eased to a sparkling 3-1 win at Plymouth as Jack Diamond scored their opener, helped set up a second for Kyle Wootton and a third for Ryan Glover before Xavier Amaechi gave Argyle a late consolation. Mansfield made a winning start with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Doncaster. Rhys Oates swept home the opener but Rovers levelled four minutes after the break when through Jack Senior before Mansfield deservedly won it in the 74th minute with a free-kick from Louis Reed. Olly Sanderson bundled home in stoppage time to snatch Stevenage a point in a 1-1 draw at Burton. The former Fulham youngster came off the bench to cancel out Jack Armer’s second-half strike for the Brewers. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Josh Coburn scored twice as Millwall kicked off their campaign with a comfortable 2-0 win over 10-man Bristol City at Ashton Gate. The home side went a man down after 36 minutes when midfielder Adam Randell was shown a second yellow card for a foul to prevent a counterattack.

Five minutes later, Coburn converted a low Ryan Leonard cross from the right with a near-post volley. Coburn then doubled the advantage after 50 minutes, taking advantage of poor defending to score unchallenged with a downward header from 10 yards.

The result meant that Skubala’s reign as City manager has begun with two home defeats, after the shock Carabao Cup exit at the hands of League Two Walsall, and without his side scoring a goal.

View image in fullscreen Josh Coburn scores Millwall’s second against Bristol City. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images

Steven Schumacher celebrated Bolton’s first Championship win for seven years after surviving a late scare against Preston. Sam Dalby and Thierry Gale put Bolton in command with first-half goals, but the Preston substitute Jusef Erabi ensured a nervy ending by pulling a goal back in the 86th minute. Liam Lindsay passed up a chance to equalise, heading over in added time, to leave Schumacher a relieved man.

“That’s what this division is all about,” he said. “From being in control of the game we’re happy they missed a sitter at the end not to take away our three points. It’s going to be an exciting ride so strap in.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Tyreece Campbell’s impressive start to the new season continued as his 80th-minute goal earned Charlton a 2-1 victory over Derby at The Valley. It capped off a week to forget for the Rams after the takeover by the Saudi government official Turki Alalshikh collapsed on Monday.

Sammie Szmodics, who scored in the EFL Cup loss to Lincoln, put Derby into a lead at the halfway point. But Lloyd Jones, who signed a new two-year contract on Friday, headed the Addicks level before Campbell produced an excellent finish to seal maximum points for the home side.

Quick Guide League Two: York return with victory Show York debutant Harry Boyes bagged a brace to mark the club’s EFL return after a 10-year absence with a thrilling 3-2 home triumph over Bristol Rovers. Boyes – a summer signing from Southend – netted the first EFL goals of his career and was joined on the Minstermen scoresheet by Alex Newby. Clinton Mola had given Steve Evans’ visitors a first-half lead and substitute Tommy Leigh later levelled from the penalty spot, but Boyes had the last say. Newport and new manager Hayden Mullins enjoyed a dream start to their League Two campaign with a 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale. First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge at a sun-baked Rodney Parade. Calum Kavanagh’s second-half double gave Oldham a 2-0 home win against relegated Port Vale. Kavanagh, who scored twice in 10 games last season after arriving from Bradford in January, struck twice in the space of 15 minutes to earn the Latics an opening-day victory. Charlie Caton scored twice but Accrington had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw with Colchester. Colchester who broke the deadlock after 24 minutes when Ellis Iandolo headed home. Stanley levelled five minutes later when Shaun Whalley’s cross was headed into the far corner by Caton. The Reds took the lead in the first minute of added time at the end of the first half as Caton in the box and he fired home. Colchester equalised on the hour when Rob Hunt’s high cross dipped straight into the top corner of the net. Goals from Oisin Gallagher, Charlie Lakin and Kabongo Tshimanga earned Barnet a 3-1 opening-day win over Salford. The trio struck to put the Bees in full control before Adebola Oluwo’s last-minute consolation. A debut strike from Leicester loanee Jake Evans sealed a 2-1 home win for Cheltenham over Rotherham. The Robins led through Charlie McCann’s first-half strike before Jili Buyabu levelled for the Millers in the 62nd minute. But Evans, who turns 18 on Friday, went on from the bench and sealed the points for Steve Cotterill’s side. Veteran striker Ched Evans scored the only goal of the game, finding the net against one of his former clubs to give Fleetwood an opening day 1-0 victory at Chesterfield. Josh March headed the winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time as 10-man Crewe got the better of nine-man Crawley at the Broadfield Stadium. Late goals from Isaac Moore, James Connolly and Aaron Pressley did the damage as Walsall secured a fine 3-0 away win over Gillingham. Grimsby got off to a winning start at the expense of newly-relegated Exeter with a tightly-contested 1-0 triumph at Blundell Park. Harvey Rodgers gave the hosts the lead 36 minutes in as he got on the end of a corner from Charles Vernam, with the linesman calling it over the line before it was cleared. Tranmere completed a 2-0 victory over Shrewsbury. Jordan Davies’ first league goal for the club and a Charlie Whitaker wonder strike secured the points in an entertaining opening-day clash at Prenton Park. Northampton and Swindon played out a goalless draw at Sixfields. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Charlton’s manager, Nathan Jones, said later that he was hoping to secure Campbell on a new contract. His current deal expires next summer. “TC gets in those positions all the time and one-v-one he is a threat. We just want the outcomes from him. We are in really advanced negotiations with him. We’re hoping we can get that done.”

Adam Idah snatched the winner with his first touch as Swansea battled back from a goal down to beat Stoke 2-1. The Republic of Ireland international had been on the pitch for barely 60 seconds when he scored in the 66th minute as the Swans claimed their first win at Stoke for more than five years. Eric Bocat had fired Stoke into a 10th-minute lead and Joseph Opoku hit a 23rd-minute equaliser for the Swans, powering in with a sweet right-foot shot after some poor defending.

Sheffield United and Birmingham made an underwhelming start to the season in a goalless draw at Bramall Lane. Both sides have ambitions of mounting promotion challenges but there was not too much to get excited about.

The only action of note in the opening half came just before the half-hour. The Blades went first as Patrick Bamford hooked Femi Seriki’s deflected cross just wide. Birmingham responded straight away and Alex Cochrane’s cross was perfect for Paik Seung-ho but the South Korean could not get enough on his header.

Birmingham had a big moment in the 58th minute when Carlos Vicente was played through on goal but his attempted pass was cut out by Japhet Tanganga when the better option was to shoot. The visitors produced the first shot on target in the 62nd minute when Jay Stansfield’s low show was kept out by Michael Cooper.

Sports.title: Scotland hope to name 39-year-old Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association hopes to name the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager early next week. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002-04.

Clarke’s abrupt departure came as Scotland exited the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager; Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand were linked with the position.

Pocognoli will probably be welcomed by Scotland fans in respect of a fresh approach. Clarke was in position for a generally successful seven years, but was often criticised for a pragmatic style.

After a period in youth coaching, Pocognoli enjoyed a successful time in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland. Under Pocognoli, Union won their first title in 90 years in 2025. A move to Monaco followed, but Pocognoli lasted eight months and 38 games in France.
