Sports.title: 'We are speechless and filled with anger': Cyclists' union vent fury and call for better helmets after death of 19-year-old British rider Finlay Tarling in tragic crash
Sports.content:
A union representing cyclists has called for better helmets following the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling.

The 19-year-old Welsh rider, who had raced for Great Britain on the road and track, died during the Volta a Portugal on Friday.

Tarling was on the eighth stage of the race when the incident occurred on a 166.8km route to Fafe, in the north of the country.

Portugal's National Republican Guard have launched an investigation into a 'collision between the cyclist and a light goods vehicle'.

The cyclists union, the Cyclistes Professionnels Associes (CPA), declared their anger in a statement on social media.

'We are speechless and filled with anger after the news of Finlay Tarling's death at the Tour of Portugal,' the statement read.

Finlay Tarling, 19, tragically died on Friday following a crash at the Tour of Portugal

'It is not right that a young athlete's life should end this way, and we are furious that even today it is still not possible to prevent such serious accidents.

'We share in the grief of his family, friends, team, and everyone who knew Finlay.

'Rest in peace, young rider; we pray for you, and we will carry you in our hearts.'

CPA president Adam Hansen, who had a lengthy professional career on the road, told the BBC that the quality of helmets used in the sport needs to improve as the average speed of racing continues to increase.

'They need a major upgrade,' Hansen said.

'Bike helmets only need to meet standard testing like all helmets, EU standard CE EN 1078 is only rated for 19.5km/h and I do not believe this is enough for road racing.'

Hansen also acknowledged the challenge faced by organisers in policing long races, which can see riders split off from the main peloton.

'The organisation is [generally] very good, but what happened [on Friday] is a bit of a hole in the system,' added Hansen.

Tarling looked to be following in the footsteps of his older brother Josh - who made his Olympic debut at Paris 2024 - as a time trial specialist

'When the breakaway or the main group goes past, sometimes the drivers [from the general public] think that's the whole race. But in fact there are riders behind and on some mountain stages the difference can be 45 minutes.

'If people do not know racing, then they just naturally think the race has past and go onto the course, where in fact there can be many groups.'

Carlos Canatario, a lieutenant in Portugal's National Republican Guard, told RTP via A Bola that Tarling had been distanced from the peloton when the incident occurred.

'It's necessary to understand this difficulty, throughout the entire race, the mobile security detail has to be systematically adapting because the peloton's configuration keeps changing,' Canatario said.

'What happened was that three cyclists began to break away from the peloton at spaced intervals, and the security detail was deploying to, as they advanced, catch up with each of the cyclists.

'Finlay Tarling was riding alongside his team's support vehicle, but as he began a descent, he gained speed and distanced himself.

'It was a combination of several factors that led to this outcome.'

Canatario also insisted the driver of the vehicle had been driving on the correct side of the road, contrary to initial reports.

'The vehicle was not going the wrong way. It was in the right lane, in its proper lane. It was going in the opposite direction to the direction of the race.

He stated that the collision occurred because 'the cyclist cut across the curve – as is natural, as cyclists do – in the leftmost lane.'

Canatario add that the driver is not expected to face criminal charges, although an investigation continues.

Tributes were paid to Tarling ahead of the ninth stage of the race on Saturday

Tarling's NSN Cycling Team pulled out of the Tour of Portugal following the tragedy

According to Portuguese media, Tarling was given immediate medical attention but died shortly after the crash. The race was neutralised about 20km from the finish line.

Tarling's team NSN said in a statement: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

'Fin was a much-loved member of our team but, most importantly, he was a son, a brother and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

'Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents, Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend.'

Tarling's older brother Josh is a world champion cyclist on the track and a stage winner at last year's Giro d'Italia. Josh made his Olympic debut at Paris 2024, where he came fourth in the men's time trial.

A statement from world governing body the UCI read: 'The UCI is deeply saddened by the tragic death of British rider Finlay Tarling, who passed away following a serious accident during today's eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

'The UCI extends its deepest condolences to Finlay's family, friends and team-mates.'

Sports.title: What happened to the last 10 Community Shield winners as curse looms over Arsenal and Man City
Sports.content:
What happened to the last 10 Community Shield winners as curse looms over Arsenal and Man City

Mirror Football takes a deep dive into the last decade of Community Shield victors ahead of Arsenal vs Manchester City

View 10 Images Arsenal and Manchester City face off in the Community Shield on Sunday (Image: Getty)

Premier League champions Arsenal face Manchester City in Sunday afternoon's FA Community Shield in Cardiff. The Gunners finally overcame their rivals to lift the league title for the first time in 22 years last season, whilst City beat Chelsea to claim the FA Cup before Pep Guardiola's summer exit.

‌



However, winning the first trophy of the season may be more of a curse than a sign of things to come.

‌



Formerly named the Charity Shield, this fixture kicks off England's domestic top-flight campaign year after year. But fans hoping their team lifts the silverware should not pay too much attention to the outcome, as history shows it is a poor barometer of a team's success for the remainder of the season.

‌



Only one team - City in 2018/19 - have gone on to win the Premier League after lifting the Community Shield in its last 10 editions. Only four of those 10 sides have won any additional silverware in the same campaign.

Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

That won't stop Maresca and Arteta from wanting to claim the shield and send a message to the other, however. City and Arsenal are the only teams to have won it three times in the past decade.

‌



Incredibly, penalties have decided six of the last 10 victors, meaning fans should expect a cagey affair as the two sides lack full match sharpness. Here, Mirror Football takes a look back at the last ten years of the Community Shield to see how each winner has fared in the season that follows.

2025 - Crystal Palace

View 10 Images Palace won the Community Shield for the first time last year (Image: Getty)

Crystal Palace claimed their first-ever Community Shield by beating Liverpool 3–2 on penalties after a 2–2 draw at Wembley Stadium. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored a penalty and Ismaila Sarr struck late for Palace, whilst Reds debutants Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong netted for Liverpool before the game was decided by a shootout.

‌



Oliver Glasner's side went on to have an underwhelming domestic campaign after key players departed, finishing 15th in the Premier League. However, they capped off an unforgettable season in Europe by lifting the UEFA Conference League trophy - the first European trophy in the club's history.

2024 - Manchester City

View 10 Images City beat rivals United on penalties in 2024 (Image: Rob Newell/CameraSport)

Manchester City defeated bitter rivals Manchester United 7–6 in a penalty shootout following a 1–1 draw at Wembley in 2024. Alejandro Garnacho gave United the lead in the 82nd minute before Bernardo Silva headed home an 89th-minute equaliser to force the shootout.

‌



Making hard work of a poor United side proved to be a sign of things to come, as Pep Guardiola's men finished third in the Premier League in 2024/25, whilst Liverpool reclaimed the league title. City reached the FA Cup final but lost 1-0 to a well-drilled Palace, meaning the Community Shield proved to be their only piece of silverware for the campaign.

Fans can watch the game live on TNT Sports via HBO Max or Prime Video's HBO Max channel.

2023 - Arsenal

View 10 Images Arteta won his second Community Shield against City (Image: Sportsphoto/Allstar)

‌



Arsenal lifted the trophy by beating Manchester City 4–1 on penalties following a 1–1 draw in normal time. Cole Palmer opened the scoring for City in the 77th minute before Leandro Trossard forced penalties with a deflected equaliser in the 101st. The shootout triumph sent the message to City that Arsenal would be serious title challengers again.

Mikel Arteta's side pushed Manchester City to the final day in the 2023/24 Premier League title race, ultimately finishing as runners-up with 89 points. Despite their strong league display, the Gunners failed to add any major trophies to their collection that season.

2022 - Liverpool

View 10 Images Liverpool won the trophy but endured a poor season (Image: Getty )

‌



Liverpool secured a 3–1 victory over Manchester City at the King Power Stadium to clinch their 16th Community Shield. Trent Alexander-Arnold opened the scoring, Mohamed Salah converted a penalty and debutant Darwin Nunez sealed the win late on, with Julian Alvarez scoring City's only goal.

However, Jurgen Klopp's men suffered their worst season in several years, finishing fifth in the Premier League due to inconsistent form and missing out on Champions League qualification. They failed to win any additional silverware, exiting early in both domestic cups and the Champions League.

2021 - Leicester City

View 10 Images The Foxes triumphed over City in 2021 (Image: Getty)

‌



FA Cup winners Leicester City unexpectedly beat Premier League champions Manchester City 1–0 to win the Community Shield for the second time in their history five years ago. Leicester's Kelechi Iheanacho scored the match-winning penalty against his former club in the 89th minute after being brought down by Nathan Ake.

The Foxes under Brendan Rodgers went on to have a solid Premier League campaign, finishing eighth. They failed to capture further domestic silverware, but did enjoy a run to the semi-finals of the inaugural Europa Conference League, marking a successful season overall.

2020 - Arsenal

View 10 Images Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang helped Arsenal win the shield six years ago (Image: Getty)

‌



FA Cup winners Arsenal defeated Premier League champions Liverpool 5–4 on penalties after a 1–1 draw at an empty Wembley Stadium. Fans were not in attendance due to COVID-19 restrictions and this 2020 trophy marked Arteta's second piece of silverware as a manager in his first year in charge.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang curled in the opening goal for Arsenal before Takumi Minamino equalised for Liverpool in the second half. However, Arteta's men struggled for domestic momentum, finishing eighth in the Premier League for a second consecutive year. They ended the season without any additional silverware after being eliminated in the Europa League semi-finals.

2019 - Manchester City

View 10 Images City beat Liverpool on penalties in 2019 (Image: Getty)

‌



Manchester City triumphed over Liverpool 5–4 in a penalty shootout at the end of a 1–1 draw in 2019. Raheem Sterling scored against his former club in the 12th minute before Joel Matip headed home a late second-half equaliser for the Reds.

Yet, City went on to surrender their Premier League crown to Liverpool, finishing as distant runners-up in the top flight during the COVID-19-affected season. Guardiola's side salvaged domestic silverware by winning the Carabao Cup for a third consecutive season with a 2–1 victory over Aston Villa just before the pandemic led to the postponement of all football .

2018 - Manchester City

Premier League centurions Manchester City beat FA Cup holders Chelsea 2–0 in a comfortable display at Wembley Stadium. Sergio Aguero grabbed headlines by scoring a goal in each half to surpass 200 total goals for the club.

‌



Guardiola's men went on to complete an unprecedented domestic treble by retaining the Premier League title with 98 points, with Liverpool finishing one point behind.

2017 - Arsenal

View 10 Images Arsene Wenger won the shield before enduring a tough final season (Image: Getty)

FA Cup holders Arsenal beat reigning Premier League champions Chelsea 4–1 on penalties following a 1–1 draw in normal time. Victor Moses gave Chelsea the lead early in the second half before Sead Kolasinac headed in a late equaliser after Pedro was sent off.

‌



Arsenal were notably poor in Arsene Wenger's final season in charge, finishing sixth in the Premier League. They reached the League Cup final but suffered a 3–0 defeat to Manchester City, ending the season without further silverware and marking rock bottom for the club during Wenger's reign. The Frenchman departed in April 2018.

2016 - Manchester United

View 10 Images 2016 was the last time United won the Community Shield (Image: Getty)

Jose Mourinho's Manchester United claimed a 2–1 victory over Premier League champions Leicester City. Jesse Lingard scored a memorable solo opener before Jamie Vardy equalised, setting up Zlatan Ibrahimovic to head in an 83rd-minute winner on his competitive United debut.

Article continues below

Under Mourinho, United finished sixth in the Premier League table but salvaged their season through knockout football. They secured a cup double by winning both the League Cup and the Europa League, clinching Champions League qualification.

Sports.title: Tonda Eckert's Spygate explanation, why Southampton didn't sack him and intern's new job
Sports.content:
Tonda Eckert's Spygate explanation, why Southampton didn't sack him and intern's new job

Southampton's Championship campaign gets underway against Watford on Sunday, with questions abound as to why Tonda Eckert is still in charge

View 3 Images Tonda Eckert is set to lead Southampton in their Championship opener despite all the Spygate fallout (Image: X/SouthamptonFC)

Tonda Eckert will be the man in the spotlight when Southampton return to Championship duties on Sunday. The Saints might have found themselves back among the heights of the Premier League this season but instead open away to Watford a week earlier.

‌



Last season's Spygate farce saw Southampton exiled from the Championship play-off final. Losing semi-finalists Middlesbrough took their place at Wembley but couldn't make it count against Hull City, who won the race for the third and final promotion place.

‌



The dust may have settled but the effects are very much still being felt today as Southampton start the season with a four-point deduction. There's also the possibility that Eckert will face a touchline ban - or worse - after being charged with misconduct by the FA.

‌



He even sat in the stands for one pre-season fixture as a trial run. Mirror Football examines the ongoing fallout from one of the biggest controversies in English football history as Southampton go again.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spygate explanation

Back in May, Boro lobbied a very serious accusation that a member of Southampton's staff had been spotted at their Rockliffe training ground recording a team session. The man in question was seen recording footage from behind a tree but fled via the adjoining golf club after he was confronted by Middlesbrough staff and refused to identify himself.

‌



Boro's suspicions proved accurate as Southampton analyst intern William Salt was found to be the man in question. The Saints were charged with breaking EFL regulations 3.4 and 127.1 and ultimately admitted to an Independent Disciplinary Commission that they had conducted similar acts of espionage prior to games against Oxford and Ipswich Town earlier that same season, having initially denied spying.

EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate READ MORE :

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal READ MORE :

An arbitration panel reached the conclusion that Southampton had launched "a contrived and determined plan from top down to gain a competitive advantage”" over their competition. However, it took some of the responsibility off the analysts who watched opposition training, surmising that they "felt pressurised" to do so.

On May 19, a full week after Southampton's play-off semi-final victory over Boro, Southampton's expulsion from the final was confirmed. Kim Hellberg's men were reinstated in their place and Eckert was left to rue his error in judgement as a dream first season at St Mary's ended in nightmarish fashion.

‌



Explaining the saga, the German made the argument he was used to similar practices being acceptable in his homeland and Italy, where he'd gained much of his coaching experience. Eckert contended that he was not aware this was against EFL laws having taken charge in his first senior role midway through the season, though that wouldn't necessarily explain why Saints analysts had been quite so covert in their operations.

"I am a young coach, I have made a mistake, and I take full responsibility," said Eckert. "I am devastated that after six months of building that relationship [with the fans] back up, the season has come to an end...come to an end that couldn’t have left us in a worse place than we are in right now."

‌



He added: "None of what has happened had any effect on the sporting performance...I hope that over time you can understand and forgive."

Eckert, 33, confirmed earlier in the summer that he had received death threats and had no choice but to involve the police. The Athletic has also reported he reached out to former England manager Gareth Southgate and the pair had a "long conversation" so that Eckert could better understand the FA's rules.

Why he's still at Saints

View 3 Images Dragan Solak has stood by Eckert - but told him not to make a similar mistake again (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

‌



Many might make the argument that Eckert's dismissal should not have been a decision that was left to Southampton's discretion. As it is, however, the south-coast side were allowed to pass judgement on the matter and ultimately decided to stick by their boss.

It wasn't just the owners who made that call, either. The Athletic recently reported the club's board surveyed the playing squad for their opinion the day after Southampton's appeal against their play-off expulsion was rejected - and the answer was that Eckert be allowed to stay on and make things right.

On the same day Saints owner Dragan Solak confirmed the club was sticking with Eckert, the latter posted a video explaining his actions. That also included an apology to the supporters for the manner in which his deception had led to the club suffering such extreme punishment.

‌



While Solak has proved forgiving over the ordeal, he isn't entirely without fury concerning Eckert's future. And the Serb has confirmed he has already warned his manager not to let something like this befall his club again as he gives him a "deserved second chance."

“I told him, ‘You almost broke my heart,'" said Solak earlier this summer. "'You do it again, you’ll kill me. The next time I see you in July, if you don’t know the EFL book of rules by heart, you can’t work for me. Because, we can’t have another mistake.' I truly hope that he will learn from this experience and he will achieve an incredible career."

Eckert's reputation among the fans may be somewhat more divided after it was ultimately his choices that led to the promotion dream crashing down last season. However, it's evident he has many backers from all sections of the club's hierarchy inside St. Mary's.

‌



Intern's new job

View 3 Images Southampton spy William Salt was identified via a photo posted on the club's official website (Image: Southampton FC)

As for Salt, he is an intern no more. In fact, his role in the debacle has led to a promotion after the Daily Mail reported he's landed himself a permanent job in Southampton's academy.

Eckert was reportedly impressed by Salt's work at the club despite his role in the Spygate mess. And they've stuck by him with a more cemented role at their Staplewood training ground.

Article continues below

Salt will presumably be permitted to continue studying under one of the hottest young coaching talents in Europe as a result. However, there's one very specific page in Eckert's book that the former intern will not be taking a leaf out of anytime soon.

Sports.title: Islam Makhachev edges Ian Machado Garry in historic win to retain world title
Sports.content:
Islam Makhachev edges Ian Machado Garry in historic win to retain world title

Islam Makhachev was made to work - but showed his championship experience to beat Ian Machado Garry in an epic welterweight dust-up

View 3 Images Islam Makhachev edged Ian Machado Garry in a welterweight thriller at UFC 330 (Image: Zuffa LLC)

Islam Makhachev was forced to show his championship experience after edging Ian Machado Garry in a thriller to retain his welterweight title.

‌



There was much more on the line for the champion than just a shiny belt. While Makhachev will undeniably go down as one of the best fighters on the planet, the Dagestan brawler was presented with the opportunity to break Anderson Silva's record (16) for the longest win streak in UFC history.

‌



But he was made to work against a young and hungry challenger in the shape of Machado Garry. After a quiet opening round - which largely saw Makhachev dominate the grappling exchanges - the welterweight dust-up exploded into life in the second after the Russian sent Machado Garry crashing to the canvas with a head kick. The move seemed to give the energetic champion the perfect opportunity to pounce in search of a stunning victory.

‌



The 170lb king immediately chased his prey, and was quick to toss the Dubliner to the canvas with ease. As the crowd made their thoughts clear with anti-Garry chants, the Irish scrapper was doing everything in his power to avoid a brutal onslaught from his adversary.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

UFC star dies aged 34 after suffering suspected heart attack READ MORE :

After a rugged display in the second, the tide seemed to turn in the third round for Machado Garry. As the challenger rushed to the centre of the octagon, the Irish scrapper fired off several kicks to keep Makhachev guessing. The young challenger was starting to get a bit of a second wind after landing multiple kicks to the body, but was momentarily halted by a takedown.

‌



The third round was by far Machado Garry's best of the night - as his versatile striking in the chaotic exchanges seemed to pay dividends. Confidence was certainly high for the 28-year-old, and it was evident that the Russian was starting to fade.

View 3 Images Machado Garry showed tremendous heart throughout the contest and pushed Makhachev to the limit (Image: Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)

Just when the fight was about to turn completely on its head, Makhachev reverted back to his bread-and-butter - his wrestling. The UFC veteran secured a high crotch before dumping Machado Garry to the canvas in a dominant fourth. With the championship showdown neck and neck, the fight was up for grabs in the final round.

‌



Conor McGregor announces return date as full extent of injury is revealed READ MORE :

Conor McGregor demands Max Holloway fight result is changed READ MORE :

As Machado Garry threatened to go in for the kill, the fight swung in favour of the champion after the Dagestani scored a much needed takedown in the closing moments of the fight. With seconds ticking away, the challenger was in search of a miracle as he fired off several shots over his shoulder, but it was not enough to deter Makhachev who sailed to the final horn.

The Russian was eventually crowned the winner - smashing Silva's historic record - with scores of 49-46, 49-46 and 48-47. “Ian is a great fighter, he gave me a hard time. But I prove every fight," said the champion.

"Oh, let’s see [if it’s the most-difficult fight I’ve had]. Maybe the first one in Australia [against Alex Volkanovski], it was also very hard. I feel the guys have more power [at 170lb], very hard to submit them, but still my game is working. I take down all my opponents and give them a hard time there."

‌



View 3 Images Makhachev's win saw him beat Anderson Silva's record for the longest win streak in UFC history (Image: Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)

A crestfallen Machado Garry - who showed plenty of promising signs - vowed to come back stronger than ever. “Nothing surprised me. I have nothing but respect for Islam," he said. "I believed in my heart and in my soul I was better than him tonight; he won, I have no complaints, no excuses.

“This was the best camp of my life. I love my wife, my little boy, I fight to make them happy. I’m 28 years of age, I have a decade of domination in this sport. This man won today, that’s okay. I’m as f***ing bulletproof as I could be up here [mentally]. To all the fans that doubt me, I’ll be back. I don’t need any of you, so go f*** yourselves!”

Article continues below

In the co-main event, Mackenzie Dern successfully defended her strawweight title in a one-sided performance against UFC veteran Gillian Robertson. Despite a late flurry from Robertson in the championship rounds, Dern won the majority of the contest - largely due to her unique and versatile arsenal.

Elsewhere on the main card, Jalin Turner made it back-to-back wins after needing just over 30 seconds to render Kaue Fernandes unconscious. Dustin Stoltzfus ended a two-fight losing skid after choking out Mansur Abdul-Malik. In the main card opener, Esteban Ribovics brutally stopped fan-favourite Edson Barboza in the second stanza.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Kim Min-jae makes transfer decision as Amorim hands former club opportunity
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Kim Min-jae makes transfer decision as Amorim hands former club opportunity

Manchester United are looking to complete more signings as the clock ticks down ahead of the summer transfer deadline

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United side are expected to be in active in the final two weeks of the transfer window

After a bright start to the summer transfer window, Manchester United's business has slowed. But there are strong signs the pace could be about to pick up again.

‌



Having spent the last couple of years bolstering their attack and defence, United's focus this summer has primarily been on midfield. Andrey Santos arrived from Chelsea for £50m, while Youri Tielemans joined from Aston Villa for £35m and it's understood Michael Carrick's side are still looking to add another central midfielder before the transfer window closes, even with the recent addition of 18-year-old Cristian Orozco.

‌



But it isn't just the centre of the park where United are looking to strengthen. The club are also considering further additions in attack and defence, with several deals reportedly in the offing as the deadline approaches.

‌



With that in mind, here are the latest Manchester United-related transfer headlines as the start of the 2026/27 Premier League season draws closer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd new signing sends message to Michael Carrick during private friendly READ MORE :

Youri Tielemans hits back at Marcus Rashford claims and speaks mind on Kobbie Mainoo READ MORE :

Kim makes Man Utd transfer decision

Manchester United's long-standing pursuit of Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae appears to have hit a brick wall. The South Korea international has reportedly made a definitive decision regarding his future amidst ongoing interest from the Red Devils.

‌



Despite falling out of favour at times under Bayern boss Vincent Kompany, the centre back remains fully committed to fighting for his place in Germany. According to BILD, the 29-year-old is more than happy with his current role and has no desire to force a move abroad.

View 3 Images Kim Min-jae has decided to stay at Bayern Munich (Image: Getty)

This marks a frustrating blow for United, who have monitored the defender closely since his title-winning days at Napoli. With the player turning 30 in November, it is now highly unlikely he will ever ply his trade at Old Trafford.

‌



Amorim hands Man Utd transfer opportunity

Elsewhere, a massive squad overhaul at AC Milan could open the door for United to finally land long-term target Christopher Nkunku. Former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim, now head coach at the San Siro, has reportedly deemed the French forward surplus to requirements after an underwhelming pre-season tour.

View 3 Images Long-term Man Utd target Christopher Nkunku is up for sale (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

United have monitored the versatile attacker for years, dating all the way back to Ralf Rangnick's tenure in 2022. A move never materialised at the time, and Nkunku eventually endured a difficult stint at Chelsea before joining the Serie A giants.

Article continues below

With Amorim now sanctioning his departure, the Old Trafford hierarchy have been presented with a golden opportunity to bolster their attacking ranks. Whether Michael Carrick's side will make a formal approach remains to be seen, but the chance to secure a long-admired talent could prove too tempting to ignore.

Sports.content:
Man City and Arsenal handed Ayyoub Bouaddi transfer update with coach admission

Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has been linked with a move to Manchester City and Arsenal during the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi has been linked with Man City and Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Lille boss Davide Ancelotti has outlined his intentions to keep Ayyoub Bouaddi at the club despite reported interest from Manchester City and Arsenal. The 18-year-old midfielder has seen his future become the subject of intense speculation ever since his impressive run of performances with Morocco at the World Cup.

‌



Reports in recent weeks have claimed that both City and the Gunners have an interest in signing Bouaddi, with suggestions that Lille have placed a €100million (£85.6million) valuation on the teenager.

‌



Saturday saw Lille face Everton in a pre-season friendly, where Bouaddi made a substitute appearance at half-time at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

‌

Sports.title: Michael Carrick sends Man Utd stars demand after AC Milan loss - 'No excuses'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick sends Man Utd stars demand after AC Milan loss - 'No excuses'

Manchester United suffered a 4-2 defeat to AC Milan in their final pre-season friendly on Saturday and Michael Carrick made no bones about their underwhelming performance

View 2 Images Michael Carrick gave an honest assessment (Image: MUTV)

Michael Carrick has told Manchester United's players that they must improve after their performance against AC Milan was 'not good enough'. The Red Devils lost their final pre-season game 4-2 against former boss Ruben Amorim's side, despite taking the lead twice through Harry Maguire and then Patrick Dorgu.

‌



Carrick had a near-full-strength squad to choose from in Wroclaw, Poland but his team faltered after he made changes on the hour mark. United's manager introduced the likes of Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez, each of whom were given their first minutes of pre-season.

‌



In an honest post-match interview, Carrick told MUTV: "We're disappointed with today. We didn't play well today. There's reasons for that in some ways [but] we need to learn from it, we need to improve.

‌



"Some of the boys were playing their first minutes. There's different reasons anyway. No excuses, we just didn't play very well today.

"But in the whole, we're ready for next week. A lot of the boys will be better for the minutes. We've done a lot of work on the training pitch ... I think the performances in the games have been pretty good. So, we're still in good spirits going into next week."

The defeat meant that United ended their pre-season campaign with three wins, one draw and two defeats. On the summer campaign, Carrick concluded: "It's been very good.

"I think there's a lot of positives to take from it. A lot of the performances, I think the group has grown and got stronger."

‌



United will now return to Manchester and prepare for their opening Premier League fixture away to newly promoted Hull City at 12:30pm next Saturday. "The boys will have a day off tomorrow and then in for the rest of the week," Carrick explained.

Carrick hopes to have both Mason Mount and Benjamin Sesko available for the clash with Hull. Mount picked up a knock last week while Sesko has been out since the end of last season with a shin injury.

After facing Hull, Carrick's side will take on another newly promoted team, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford. It's then a trip to Everton, a home derby against Manchester City and a visit to Fulham before the international break.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala collapses during Bayern Munich match as teammate forced into action to catch him
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala collapses during Bayern Munich match as teammate forced into action to catch him

Bayern Munich were in pre-season action with a worrying moment for the forward.

View 3 Images Jamal Musiala was caught by teammate Ismael Saibari after appearing unsteady on his feet. (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala had to be caught by teammate Ismael Saibari as he appeared to pass out during the team’s pre-season friendly. The German giants hosted RB Leipzig as they continue their preparations for the new season.

‌



The match was played in 33-degree heat, which appeared to be too much for Musiala in the closing stages after coming on as a second-half substitute. The incident came in the moments after he effectively sealed the game for Bayern.

‌



Just minutes after the goal, the forward started to appear disoriented. That was noticed by Saibari, who rushed to help his new teammate.

‌

Both Saibari and Joshua Kimmich were able to catch Musiala before he fell to the ground, and slowly lowered him to the deck. Medics were on the scene to provide immediate treatment as teammates gathered around.

In good news, a thumbs up was given towards the bench from a medic. Musiala was then able to get up and walk off the pitch alongside members of the Bayern medical team as he was replaced by Bara Sapoko Ndiaye.

‌



It was a dramatic introduction to Bayern Munich for Saibari, who made his debut for the club after completing a transfer from PSV Eindhoven earlier in the summer. The midfielder has joined up with Bayern after representing Morocco in this summer’s World Cup in North America.

View 3 Images Ismael Saibari rushed to help teammate Jamal Musiala. (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Bayern came out as 3-1 winners, thanks to goals from Luis Diaz, Nathaniel Brown and Musiala, a goal which was assisted by Saibari.

‌



Speaking in the mixed zone following the win, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl provided an update on Musiala, confirming: "The most important thing, he's doing well!"

View 3 Images Jamal Musiala was able to walk off the pitch after receiving medical attention. (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Bayern also suffered two other injury worries throughout the game with full-back Konrad Laimer forced off after just 10 minutes. Centre-back Min-jae Kim was then replaced during the second-half hydration break.

‌



Giving an update on Laimer, Eberl said: "Konny took a hit relatively early on, and his foot swelled up pretty quickly as well.

"That's why he was taken off as a precaution. It was already the case that he couldn't run anymore; he had to be supported. That was visible. He wasn't running smoothly at all. How long it will take, I really can't say today."

Bayern Munich are back in action next Saturday when they take on Borussia Dortmund in the German Super Cup final. Their season opener in the Bundesliga comes on Friday, 28 August vs VfB Stuttgart.

Sports.title: Norwich City boss fumes after officials ALLOW handball goal - 'Shouldn't happen'
Sports.content:
Norwich City boss fumes after officials ALLOW handball goal - 'Shouldn't happen'

Norwich City were beaten 2-1 by West Bromwich Albion in their Championship opener on Saturday afternoon but there are question marks over Aune Heggebo's opening goal

View 2 Images Aune Heggebo's goal for West Brom in their win over Norwich seemed to go in off his arm

Norwich head coach Philippe Clement was left feeling extremely hard done by after watching his side lose 2-1 at home to West Brom in their opening Championship fixture.

‌



Clement felt his side should have won the game comfortably with the number of chances they created – and also felt Aune Heggebo’s opener, which came against the run of play, should have been ruled out for handball.

‌



“It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,” he said. “It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted.

‌



“There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn’t have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that. Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn’t happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.”

As for his side’s performance, he added: “We should have won this game, we played well, showed good intensity and were the better side in all aspects of the game. I am really pleased with all aspects of the performance – except putting the ball in the back of the net.”

‌



Norwich were on the front foot for most of the game but could not find a way past a resolute defence, with a series of last-ditch blocks, and some excellent stops from Max O’Leary, keeping them at bay.

And they were made to pay for failing to take their chances as Albion scored two late goals to make it a dream start to the new Championship season.

The visitors went in front on 75 minutes when Callum Styles played in Jimmy-Jay Morgan, whose cross was bundled over the line by Heggebo. With three minutes remaining, Morgan made it two with his third goal since joining the Baggies in the summer, racing clear and working his way into the box before blasting the ball home.

‌



View 2 Images Heggebo's goal was the first of two late strikes scored by West Brom as they ran out 2-1 winners at Carrow Road (Image: Adam Fradgley/West Bromwich Albion FC)

Mathias Kvistgaarden nodded home a loose ball as the game entered added time, after a shot from Jacob Wright had been brilliantly saved, but it was too little, too late for Norwich.

West Brom manager James Morrison admitted his side were fortunate to come away with all three points. “We were on the defensive for a lot of the game and certainly rode our luck at times,” he said. “We weren’t good enough on the ball, especially in the first half.

‌



“We certainly didn’t play the sort of football we did in pre-season. We need to be a lot better than this, although I am sure we will be better once we get into our rhythm.

“In the end we were grateful for some good saves from Max (O’Leary), some good blocks – and a lot of hard work.

“We improved a bit after the break, and I think the substitutions helped and it was obviously pleasing to get those late goals.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
